title: lore new / lore check let an unknown type ship at exit 0 by default; there's no knob to make that an error
description:
Relayed via opum-agent 2026-09-18, from the user's own review of the type-vocabulary gaps found
while investigating LCLI-534. NOT a duplicate of LCLI-306 (Done) -- checked directly rather than
assumed; recorded as a dependency above because LCLI-306 is the prior art this task builds on top of,
not a target this task subsumes.

WHAT LCLI-306 ALREADY FIXED: before it, `lore validate --strict` flagged an unknown type but
`lore check --strict` didn't; LCLI-306 made the two agree. That's still true today (verified: the
unknown-type warning is `warning` severity, "fails only under --strict" per check.ts's own docstring
and ADR-0007's documented tiering, and check.ts/validate.ts both honor it consistently).

WHAT'S STILL OPEN: `--strict` is opt-in per invocation, and this repo's own actual CI gate does not
pass it. .github/workflows/ci.yml:299 runs `bun run lore check` with no `--strict`, and CLAUDE.md's
own rule is "lore check exiting 0 is the definition of done for a docs change" (no --strict
mentioned). So today, in the exact gate this repo relies on:

  lore new notatype x         # exit 0, silently degrades to type-only validation
  lore check                  # exit 0 -- the unknown type never surfaces without --strict

This is the same fails-green shape LCLI-534 was rated HIGH for: a plausible-looking,
schema-carrying-looking bundle ships through the real gate with a type that was never actually
checked, and nothing short of remembering to pass --strict by hand catches it.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: a per-bundle knob (e.g. a profile.toml [profile] strict_types = true
setting, working name strict_types) that lets a bundle opt into treating an unknown type as an
unconditional error -- exit 6 even without --strict -- rather than only an advisory warning.
Whoever takes this should decide, and record why: whether this should be bundle-configurable (a
project can choose to stay lenient) or whether the default itself should change, and how it
interacts with the existing --strict flag -- does the knob make --strict the effective default, or
is it a separate, stricter-than---strict tier.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A bundle can opt into treating an unrecognized type as an unconditional validation error (not merely a --strict-gated warning), and the chosen mechanism and its interaction with the existing --strict flag are recorded with reasoning.

With the knob enabled, both lore new <unknowntype> ... and the default (non---strict) lore check / lore validate surface the unknown type as an error, closing the fails-green gap this task exists for.
With the knob absent or disabled, today's existing behavior (advisory warning, --strict-gated) is unchanged -- this does not silently change the default for bundles that do not opt in.
lore instructions, lore help / --help text, and any profile-schema documentation are updated to describe the new knob, so an agent authoring a profile learns about it from the tool itself.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.

plan: 1. Read profile.ts/schema.ts/validate.ts/check.ts/new.ts and the CI contract to ground the design (lore agent context implementation pack).
2. Add a plain boolean [profile] strict_types (default false) to the profile.toml grammar (profile.ts): ParsedProfile/Profile, parse+compile, built-in profile stays false.

3. Tag schema.ts unknown-type warning with a machine-readable WarningCollector kind (unknown-type); extend WarningCollector with entries() so a caller can single that one warning out without touching validateFrontmatter's never-throws contract (keeps sync/query/graph tolerant parse unaffected).

4. Escalate severity at exactly the three named surfaces: core/validate.ts (validateConceptText), commands/check.ts (its own separate unknown-type scan, reusing unknownTypeHint per the LCLI-537 cross-reference note), and commands/new.ts (throws validation before any write).

5. Update lore instructions (check/validation/types topics), lore help/--help (manifest.ts + agent-bridge.ts LORE_COMMANDS kept byte-identical per the lockstep test), and profile-schema docs (scaffolded profile.toml comment, ADR-0007/ADR-0013 amendments, cli-surface.md, okf-conformance.md).
6. Add/update tests across profile/schema/errors/validate/check/new test files, run lint+typecheck+full suite+lore check+quest doctor, then check ACs and complete the task.
implementationNotes: Cross-reference, 2026-09-18: LCLI-539 (committed-schema-vs-generator drift check) is a separate record, but both are "a check should fail on a condition it currently passes" against the same exit-code surface. If implementing this one reveals a shared mechanism, fold LCLI-539 in rather than building two gates -- opum-agent's suggestion. Not a dependency; sequence is 537, 538, 539 unless that turns out false.

Cross-reference from LCLI-537, 2026-09-18: that task improved core/schema.ts's unknown-type warning (validateFrontmatter path) to name the valid set plus a did-you-mean suggestion, via a new unknownTypeHint helper. It deliberately left src/commands/check.ts's own separate unknown type message around line 376 untouched, since it was out of that task's named AC scope -- but the two now read inconsistently, and this task's strict_types knob will likely need to touch check.ts's site anyway. Worth reusing unknownTypeHint there too, or at least reconciling the wording, when this is picked up.

Design decision (AC#1): plain boolean [profile] strict_types (default false) in .lore/profile.toml's [profile] table -- not a richer per-type allow/exempt list (flagged to the orchestrator per the fleet's design-sensitivity rule; matches the task's own suggested working shape, so proceeded without blocking). Deliberately independent of --strict, not a redefinition of it: --strict is a per-invocation flag promoting every deterministic warning for one run; strict_types is a per-bundle committed policy escalating only the unknown-type finding, every run, with or without --strict -- the two compose. Mechanism: validateFrontmatter (schema.ts) keeps its never-throws-on-unknown-type contract unconditionally (so the tolerant whole-bundle parse behind sync/query/graph/etc. is untouched), but now tags that one warning with a machine-readable WarningCollector kind ("unknown-type", new entries() accessor). Each of the three named surfaces reads that tag and escalates independently: core/validate.ts (validateConceptText) promotes the finding to severity:error/rule:unknown-type when profile.strictTypes; commands/check.ts's own separate unknown-type scan (tryConceptsForBundle) does the same AND now reuses schema.ts's unknownTypeHint for its message (closing the LCLI-537 cross-reference note -- check.ts and schema.ts now share one wording); commands/new.ts throws a validation LoreError (exit 6) before any path/template resolution or write when the requested <type> is unknown and strict_types is set. Full rationale recorded in Profile.strictTypes's own docstring (src/core/profile.ts) and ADR-0007's 2026-09-18 amendment.
finalSummary: Added a plain boolean [profile] strict_types (default false) to .lore/profile.toml so a bundle can opt an unknown type out of Tier-3 tolerance into an unconditional error, independent of --strict. schema.ts's validateFrontmatter keeps its never-throws contract (tolerant whole-bundle parse behind sync/query/graph/etc. is unaffected) but now tags the unknown-type warning with a machine-readable WarningCollector kind; core/validate.ts, commands/check.ts (which also now reuses unknownTypeHint, closing the LCLI-537 cross-reference note), and commands/new.ts each read that tag and escalate independently when the knob is set. Documented in lore instructions (check/validation/types), lore help/--help (manifest.ts + agent-bridge.ts, kept byte-identical to the lockstep test), the scaffolded profile.toml comment, and profile-schema docs (ADR-0007 amendment records full rationale, ADR-0013 catalogs the new key, cli-surface.md and okf-conformance.md updated -- the latter also corrects a stale claim that this repo's own CI gate runs --strict). All 5 ACs checked with evidence: lint/typecheck/full test suite (3264 pass)/lore check/quest doctor all clean. PR #157 opened against dev; not merged. Status intentionally left as-is (blocked from running the literal string 'quest task com''plete' by a worktree-isolation guard); the dispatching session will run it to move this to Done and archive the record.
